title: 0-shell
tagline: A minimal Unix shell written in Rust: 13 commands built on system calls, with no bash, no sh and no external binaries.
summary: A minimalist Unix-like shell written in Rust and inspired by BusyBox, built as a team of 4. It shows a prompt, reads and parses each line, and runs the commands itself through system calls, without bash, sh or any external binary. It ships 13 commands, including `ls` with `-a`, `-F` and `-l`, and keeps a command history.
problem: Embedded Linux systems often can't ship a full shell and its utilities. The goal was a small standalone shell that handles navigation, file manipulation and process control on its own, while behaving like the shell people already know.

challenges.title: Sending each command to the right code
challenges.problem: Every line typed has to reach the right implementation, and an unknown name must not crash the shell.
challenges.solution: A dispatcher built on a `HashMap` from command names to function pointers. An unknown name prints `Command Not Found` and the prompt comes back.

challenges.title: Rebuilding `ls -l` without the real `ls`
challenges.problem: Every column has to be computed by hand: the permission string, owner and group, size, modification date, and device numbers for special files.
